title: Check If All 1's Are at Least Length K Places Away
statement:
You get an array `nums` made only of 0s and 1s, and an integer `k`. Decide whether every two consecutive 1s in `nums` have at least `k` zeros between them; that is, for any two 1s at indices `i < j`, the count `j - i - 1` of positions strictly between them is never below `k`.

Return `true` when this holds for every pair of 1s (including when the array has fewer than two 1s), and `false` otherwise.
notes:
## Intuition

Comparing every pair of 1s would work but costs O(n²). Only neighbouring 1s matter: if each 1 is far enough from the previous 1, any two 1s further apart are even more distant. So one left-to-right scan that remembers where the last 1 was is enough.

## Approach

1. Set `last = -1` to mean that no 1 has been seen yet.
2. Walk through `nums` with index `i` and skip every 0.
3. At a 1, if an earlier 1 exists, count the zeros between them as `i - last - 1`. If that is below `k`, return `false` at once.
4. Record `i` as the new `last`.
5. If the scan ends without a violation, return `true`.

## Example 1, step by step

`nums = [1,0,0,0,1,0,0,1]`, `k = 2`. At `i = 0` there is no earlier 1, so `last = 0`. At `i = 4` the gap is `4 - 0 - 1 = 3`, which is at least 2, so `last = 4`. At `i = 7` the gap is `7 - 4 - 1 = 2`, still at least 2, so `last = 7`. The scan finishes and the answer is `true`.

## Complexity

- Time: O(n): each element is visited once.
- Space: O(1): only `last` and the loop index are kept.

## Pitfalls

- The distance asked for is the number of zeros between the 1s, `i - last - 1`, not the index difference `i - last`.
- Do not measure from index `-1` before the first 1; guard with `last !== -1`.
- With `k = 0` adjacent 1s are fine, so the answer is always `true`.
- An array with zero or one 1 has no pair to violate the rule and returns `true`.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `last` | index of the most recent 1, or `-1` before any |
| `i` | current index in `nums` |

narration.2: No 1 has been seen yet, so last starts at -1.
narration.4: Scan the array from left to right.
narration.5: A 0 cannot break the rule, so it needs no work.
narration.6: Skip straight to the next index.
narration.8: At a 1 with an earlier 1, count the zeros between them and compare with k.
narration.9: Too few zeros between these two 1s, so the answer is false.
narration.11: Remember this 1 as the latest one for the next comparison.
narration.13: Every neighbouring pair of 1s was far enough apart.
